name: Chrome plating
summary: A thin layer of chromium is put on steel by electrolysis. The layer gives a hard, bright surface that does not tarnish.
how: Clean the steel part and plate it with copper and nickel.
Put the part in a chromic acid bath and pass a current through it.
Buff the part to a mirror finish.

origin.note: Colin Fink and Charles Eldridge at Columbia University develop the bath that makes bright chromium coats.

adoptions.via: Chrome plate gives costume jewels a bright, cheap, white-metal shine.
Chrome replaces nickel on the radiator shell and the lamps of the grand car.
Chrome strips follow the flow of the body.
Bumpers, grilles and fins carry large amounts of chrome.
Chrome stays on the grille and the bumper of the muscle car.
Chrome returns on revived models as a sign of the past.
